rounds.text: Aarti Drugs Ltd is currently trading at an attractive valuation discount relative to its peers, with a trailing P/E of 19.9x [E1] and 20.07x against a sector benchmark of 31.08x [E6], alongside a lower EV/EBITDA of 13.37x compared to the 16.53x sector benchmark [E11]. Fundamental momentum is clearly accelerating, backed by a 15% TTM sales growth [E17], 16% TTM profit growth [E21], and a striking quarterly operating margin expansion of +3 percentage points to 16% in Sep 2026 [E31]. This operational turnaround is strongly supported by quality earnings, demonstrated by a robust cash conversion of 1.30x where profits are fully backed by cash [E34] and Rs 254 Cr in operating cash flow for Mar 2026 [E35]. Institutional confidence is swelling as domestic holdings climbed to 10.24% in Sep 2026 from 5.26% in Dec 2023 [E43], driving positive money flow [E44] while the stock maintains exceptional relative strength of 97 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Furthermore, the healthcare sector provides a supportive macroeconomic tailwind with a score of +0.85 [E74], enhancing the case for re-rating. Conceded: [E45], [E46], [E61], [E62].

Aarti Drugs Ltd carries significant valuation and structural risks that the current price of ₹503—sitting near 88% to 92% of its 52-week range [E5, E48]—fails to support. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at a mere Rs 278 per share, resulting in a severe negative margin of safety of -81.2% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, historical long-term growth has been lackluster, highlighted by a poor 5-year compounded sales growth of 4% and a negative 3-year compounded sales growth of -2% [E15, E16], accompanied by a 5-year compounded profit growth of -7% [E19]. Compounded share price growth over the same 5-year horizon has similarly lagged at -1% [E23], signaling that the stock's recent price-led momentum has detached from underlying multi-year fundamentals [E56]. Operational risks are compounded by rising borrowings reaching Rs 620 Cr in Sep 2026 up from Rs 577 Cr previously [E39], steady promoter selling with holdings declining from 57.47% to 54.07% [E41], and warning flags regarding potential capitalization of interest costs [E63]. conceded: [E31]

The bear's reliance on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 278 ignores immediate fundamental acceleration, where trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged by 15% and profit growth reached 16% [E17, E21], alongside quarterly net profit leaping 84% year-over-year [E68]. While multi-year growth figures from past cycles look soft, recent operational metrics show a clear turnaround with quarterly operating margins expanding to 16%—a 3 percentage point increase over the prior year—supported by an "Increasing" trend over the last four quarters [E31, E33]. The accusation of detached momentum is countered by robust cash backing, proven by a cash conversion ratio of 1.30x and Rs 254 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026, meaning profits are fully realized in cash [E34, E35]. Institutional confidence is actively building rather than fleeing, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their stake by nearly 5 percentage points to 10.24% and positive institutional money flow [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the healthcare sector backdrop is explicitly in a tailwind with a score of +0.85 [E72, E74], and valuation multiples remain discounted relative to the broader sector, trading at a P/E of 19.9x versus a sector benchmark of 31.08x and an EV/EBITDA of 13.37x against a sector benchmark of 16.53x [E1, E6, E11]. conceded: [E39, E41]

The bull leans heavily on recent TTM and quarterly acceleration, but glosses over the multi-year decay where 5-year sales growth languishes at 4% and 3-year growth turned negative at -2% [E15, E16]. While the bull cites margin expansion and cash flow [E31, E34, E35], it ignores that borrowings have simultaneously risen to Rs 620 Cr from Rs 577 Cr and that the company has been flagged for potentially capitalizing interest costs [E39, E63]. The bull highlights institutional accumulation [E43, E44], but omits the simultaneous insider dilution where promoter holdings fell from 57.47% to 54.07% [E41]. The assertion that valuation is discounted relative to sector benchmarks [E6, E11] masks the fundamental reality that a DCF model places intrinsic value at Rs 278 against a market price of Rs 503, leaving an alarming -81.2% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the bull fails to defend against the historical vulnerability of a -94.6% peak-to-trough drawdown and high annualised volatility of 44.7% [E53, E54]. conceded: [E17, E21, E31, E68]

The multi-year decay cited by the bear is superseded by a dynamic turnaround where trailing twelve-month sales growth hit 15% and profit growth reached 16%, supported by an impressive rules-based screen score of 80 out of 100 [E15, E16, E17, E21, E65]. The rise in borrowings to ₹ 620 Cr [E39] is fully backed by robust cash generation, evidenced by ₹ 254 Cr in operating cash flow and a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.30x for March 2026 [E34, E35]. While promoter holdings adjusted to 54.07% [E41], domestic institutions aggressively stepped in by increasing their stake to 10.24% from 5.26%, driving positive institutional money flow [E43, E44]. The bear's reliance on a static DCF model [E45] ignores current market reality where the stock trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a stellar relative-strength rating of 97 against the Nifty 500 [E50, E51]. Furthermore, the healthcare sector backdrop provides a powerful tailwind with a score of +0.85, matching strong sector fundamentals [E72, E74]. conceded: [E39, E41, E45, E53]

The bull points to TTM sales and profit recoveries [E17, E21], but ignores that multi-year compounded growth shows a 5-year sales crawl of 4% [E15], a 3-year sales contraction of -2% [E16], and a 5-year profit drop of -7% [E19]. While the bull cites a strong cash conversion of 1.30x [E34], it glosses over the underlying risk that borrowings expanded to ₹ 620 Cr alongside a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E39, E63]. The bull highlights institutional inflows [E43, E44], but this fails to negate the persistent promoter divestment down to 54.07% alongside a recent quarterly reduction [E41, E60]. Dismissing the DCF model [E45] as static ignores its stark warning of an -81.2% margin of safety and a valuation that requires unproven 8.3% earnings growth [E46, E47]. Finally, celebrating technical momentum and sector tailwinds [E50, E51, E72] completely evades the core structural reality of a low 3-year average return on equity of 13.3% and a steep historical drawdown risk of -94.6% [E53, E62]. conceded: [E17, E21, E34, E43, E44, E50, E51, E72]
